answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a witnessed season at a smithy forge: a licensed master smith takes one apprentice per season and forges a uniquely serial-numbered umber-steel tool for that apprentice, logged in a public registry. Random live checks summon the holder to work that forge on camera within hours, so one operator cannot staff two forges at once. The apprenticeship fee in outside money spirals upward, doubling per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real forge season, another smith's slot, another human, and twice the prior fee.
